definition: The natural logarithm of a token's predicted probability, commonly used instead of raw probability for numerical stability and easier aggregation across a sequence.
details: Log probabilities are summed rather than multiplied across a sequence to compute overall sequence likelihood, avoiding the numerical underflow that would occur when multiplying many small probabilities together.
story: Imagine a chef tasting every ingredient before it goes into the pot, deciding what belongs and what would ruin the broth. Better ingredients make a better meal, and the same is true here. Every machine is shaped by what it was shown, so someone has to choose that material with care. It is the raw material; the model is only ever as good as what it was fed. And that is Log Probability — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.
